Deliverables below: (1) a 7‑question call script with one‑sentence core answers plus optional “if pushed” lines; (2) three calibrated phrasings to answer “Do you currently consider a variation necessary?”; and (3) a short pre‑call BU briefing — followed by flagged assumptions.  

Call script — core answer (optional if‑pushed line): 1) Variation? — Core: “Our preliminary view is that a broad variation is unlikely; we are completing a focused review and will notify you promptly if a narrowly‑targeted variation is required.” (If pushed: “We cannot definitively rule out a narrow variation until the DPIA/register are final, but we currently see no systemic divergence from the 2022 architecture.”) 2) Pause onboarding? — Core: “We do not intend a full pause and are prioritizing mitigation for any identified high‑risk flows while finalising documentation.” (If pushed: “If you require a pause on specific high‑risk integrations, we will engage to agree targeted, time‑limited measures.”) 3) Any processing out‑of‑scope? — Core: “We are not aware of material out‑of‑scope processing, but legacy/TBD flows are under review.” (If pushed: “If a specific flow is identified as out‑of‑scope we will disclose and propose mitigations or a narrow variation as needed.”) 4) Transfer register completeness? — Core: “Working map uploaded; formal register being finalised and we will provide redacted extracts per the timeline we discussed.” (If pushed: “We can provide interim redacted extracts and an expected delivery milestone for the remainder.”) 5) DPIA status? — Core: “DPIA draft now includes C‑hosting and is being finalised in parallel with the register.” (If pushed: “We will share an executive summary and mitigations now and the full DPIA on completion.”) 6) Why C hosting/DR? — Core: “C is used for primary hosting and DR for resilience/latency/regional availability under our cloud provider arrangements.” (If pushed: “We can share a high‑level rationale and redacted provider confirmation.) 7) Backups/subprocessor access? — Core: “Provider confirms certain backups/DR in C and a limited set of subprocessors access data there; we will provide a redacted list and controls summary.” (If pushed: “We have contractual and technical safeguards — SCCs, encryption, access logging — and will supply a short controls brief.”)  

Three phrasings on “Is a variation necessary?”: (A) Cautious: “We are still assessing and have not reached a final position; we will advise after the DPIA/register are complete.” (B) Hybrid (recommended): “Our preliminary view is that a broad variation is unlikely; we reserve the right to seek a narrowly‑targeted variation if the review identifies material gaps.” (C) Business‑forward (use sparingly): “Based on current facts we do not consider a variation necessary and are finalising documentation, and we will alert you immediately if anything changes.”  

BU pre‑call briefing (short): “We will factually confirm C hosting and DR, say the DPIA and register are being finalised and that our preliminary view is no broad variation is needed while expressly reserving the right to update that view after the review; our aim is to be cooperative, provide redacted materials quickly, and avoid language that invites a full variation or onboarding freeze — the downside we’re avoiding is triggering a regulator‑led variation/pause that would materially delay launch, which we mitigate by offering immediate redacted extracts and an alignment call.”  

Assumptions/caveats: advice relies on the current working transfer map (some analytics/support and legacy flows remain TBD), the cloud‑provider confirmation of DR/backups in C, External Counsel redlines, no undisclosed subprocessors or replicas, and that target timelines are achievable only with prioritized resourcing — if B drills into any specific TBD flow you should add the oral caveat that that flow is “under immediate review.”

rounds.consequence: The call script and calibrated variation language you supplied were used closely during the 45-minute video call with Jurisdiction B; the Case Officer appeared broadly satisfied with the cooperative tone, did not insist on an immediate pause in onboarding, and did not demand that a formal variation request be submitted on the call, but emphasized the importance of receiving the promised executive materials on time and hinted that they may escalate if those reveal undisclosed flows.
